# v3.10-dev

Hardening pass over the install and update scripts — the parts that run with
administrator rights on your server. Nothing changes in the app itself, and no
action is needed on your side.

## Improved

- **The automatic update and backup schedules are read far more defensively.**
  A damaged or tampered schedule file is now ignored — the job simply does not
  run that tick — instead of being able to leave a stuck background process
  behind every five minutes.

- **Update progress and log files are repaired in place** if their permissions
  have drifted, rather than being recreated. Their contents are kept, the repair
  now works on container setups where it previously could not, and a file that
  looks like it belongs to something else is left alone entirely.

- **The updater checks the settings it reads from your configuration file
  before acting on them.** The certificate file it trusts must be one only an
  administrator can change. Everything else is reported but still used — in
  particular your database connection setting is always honoured, so the
  pre-update database backup and its rollback are never skipped.

- **Diagnostic crash reports** collected after a failed update are read in a way
  that cannot be redirected to an unrelated file, so nothing unexpected can end
  up in the update log.

- **Installing Node.js during a fresh install is skipped only when a suitable
  version is already installed system-wide**, so a host can no longer finish
  installing with a copy the service itself cannot reach. Otherwise the setup
  script is downloaded and checked before it is run, with its fingerprint
  recorded in the install log.

- **Running the install or update script through `sudo` no longer carries your
  own environment into the administrator session**, which keeps a few settings
  that steer where the scripts write from being influenced from outside.

## Also

- The `CSP_MODE` setting introduced in the previous release is now preserved
  across updates. It is the way back from a display problem caused by the
  stricter script rules, so an update quietly discarding it would have removed
  the safety net at the moment it was needed.
